name: Vaccines & Acute Bronchitis
cards: Everyone 6 months or older, every year, without a contraindication.
Influenza vaccine timing for most adults?
September or October; keep vaccinating while influenza circulates.
Influenza vaccine to avoid in pregnancy?
An inactivated or recombinant vaccine, any trimester.
Egg allergy and the influenza vaccine?
No egg-free product or extra precautions needed.
Preferred influenza vaccines at 65 or older?
High-dose inactivated, adjuvanted inactivated, or recombinant.
Two seasonal doses about 6 months apart.
Tdap (tetanus, diphtheria, acellular pertussis) in pregnancy?
Every pregnancy, preferably early in weeks 27 to 36.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine that completes the series alone?
PPSV23 (23-valent polysaccharide), usually 1 year or more later.
Pneumococcal vaccine: all adults from what age?
All adults 75 or older; adults 50 to 74 at increased risk.
Adult Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b) vaccine: main indication?
A virus (self-limited infection of the large airways).
Acute bronchitis: how long does the cough last?
Green or yellow sputum in bronchitis means?
None: no blood count, sputum culture or chest film.
Abnormal vital signs, focal lung findings or risk suggesting pneumonia.
No, regardless of cough duration or sputum color.
Avoid routinely: sedation, respiratory depression, misuse.
No routine systemic or inhaled corticosteroids.
Bronchitis with wheeze: what may help?
A short bronchodilator trial (then reassess for asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease).
Paroxysmal cough, post-tussive vomiting, whoop or exposure; don't wait 4 weeks.

name: Pneumonia: Scores, Types & Antibiotics
cards: Cruises and hotels, hot tubs, fountains.
Pneumonia exam: percussion over the lobe?
Pneumonia Severity Index, plus clinical judgment.
Systolic below 90 or diastolic 60 or less.
Low severity: home, unless other reasons to admit.
High severity: hospital; consider critical care at 4 or 5.
Pneumonia Severity Index class IV points?
Macrolide alone for outpatient pneumonia when?
Only if local pneumococcal resistance is below 25%.
Beta-lactam plus azithromycin or doxycycline, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.
Beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
Usual hospital or ventilator pneumonia course?
Prevention (early extubation, head of bed up, mouth care).
Pneumonitis is sterile chemical injury; pneumonia is bacterial infection.
Like breathing across an open jar (a large cavity).
Why reserve clindamycin for lung abscess?

name: Fungal, Atypical & Viral
cards: Most common opportunistic infection in HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)?

Pneumocystis: check before primaquine or dapsone?
Room-air arterial oxygen below 70 mm Hg.
CD4 below 100 (or 100 to 200 with detectable virus).
Doxycycline, 10 to 14 days after fever resolves.
Influenza type that is more pathogenic?
Gradual surface protein changes: why vaccines update yearly.
Reassortment of two strains in one host: novel strains.
Rapid molecular assay or reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction.
Still start it in high-risk or severe illness.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, severe immunosuppression, hospitalized patients.
Asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Nucleic acid amplification test (including polymerase chain reaction).
Repeat after 48 hours (2 tests if symptomatic, 3 if not).
